author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be opened with its current date and description, changed, and saved in place under the same rules booking passes. The pet gains no extra visit, and a refusal shows the form again. Cancelling stays out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when it is opened for correction, then its current date and description are shown ready to change
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit carries them and the owner's record is shown
given a pet with one booked visit, when that visit is corrected, then the pet still has exactly one visit
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused and the description is named
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused and the date is named
given a refused correction, when the refusal is shown, then the visit is offered again for a further attempt and the stored visit is unchanged
given a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet that does not belong to the named owner, when a correction is attempted, then it is refused
non_goals: cancelling a booked visit — NG-5 keeps it out of scope
a link to the correction from the owner's record — the owner deferred a visible entry point to a possible follow-up request
deleting a visit — NG-4 is untouched
changing anything on a visit other than its date and description
correcting a visit through any surface other than the correction form
notes: Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records on the log, nothing to audit. Two open questions are recorded in docs/prd.md rather than raised: whether the owner's record should later link to the correction, and whether a visit whose date has passed should be correctable. The narrowest reading is recorded meanwhile — one date rule for every visit, so a past visit only saves with a date later than today (Visits edge case 4). The ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md for adr/2026-08-21-non-goal-visit-correction.md is outside this agent's write scope; system-design-expert owns that file.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction is the create-or-update form pattern this codebase already runs twice. PetController serves both /pets/new and /pets/{petId}/edit from one controller by declaring its @ModelAttribute factory with an optional path variable (findPet takes @PathVariable(name = "petId", required = false) Integer petId, returning a new Pet when absent and owner.getPet(petId) when present). VisitController needs the same one adjustment: loadPetWithVisit gains an optional visitId and returns the existing visit from pet.getVisits() when it is present, instead of always constructing a Visit and attaching it to the pet. Everything else the slice needs is in place — the shared template posts to the current URL with no th:action, the date rule and the @NotBlank description rule already live where booking uses them, and the write path is owner-graph cascade through OwnerRepository. No new package, type, layer, or dependency. Basis: direct read of PetController.java lines 68-86 and VisitController.java lines 63-112; the IntelliJ oracle is not connected in this run, so this is the weaker file-read basis rather than a symbol resolution. docs/system-design.md Contracts now carries REQ-VISITEDIT-001 on Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, and VisitController.
integration_points: VisitController gains GET and POST on /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, both rendering pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm on the visit model attribute the intake named
loadPetWithVisit becomes the single resolution point for both routes: owner by id, pet by owner.getPet(petId), and on the correction route the visit by id from pet.getVisits()

the correction POST reuses the booking rules verbatim — the @NotBlank description on Visit plus the controller's non-future date rejection with code typeMismatch.visitDate — and redirects to redirect:/owners/{ownerId} on success
persistence stays on the existing path: the bound visit is already inside the pet's collection, so this.owners.save(owner) cascades the update and no new repository is introduced
the existing @InitBinder disallowing id and *.id already covers the correction form; no binder change is needed

patterns.description: findPet — the project's create-or-update pattern: one @ModelAttribute factory with an optional path variable, new instance when absent, aggregate lookup when present. Copy this shape into loadPetWithVisit.
getPet(Integer) — aggregate traversal by identity, skipping unsaved members. The visit lookup on the pet mirrors it.
the non-future date rejection the correction POST must apply unchanged

risks.risk: loadPetWithVisit today ends with 'Visit visit = new Visit(); pet.addVisit(visit);'. It runs before every handler in the controller, so letting the correction route fall through it attaches a second visit to the pet and breaks the acceptance criterion that the pet gains no extra visit.
risks.mitigation: Branch on visitId at the top of the factory. On the correction path return the visit found on the pet and never call addVisit; on the booking path keep the existing two lines untouched. The pet-still-has-one-visit test is the guard.

risks.risk: A refused correction must leave the stored visit unchanged, but binding mutates the loaded entity in place before validation runs.
risks.mitigation: Nothing flushes it today: findById returns a detached graph, spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled, and the refusal path returns the view without calling save. Keep the handler out of a transaction and do not add saveAndFlush on the refusal path. Assert the stored visit is unchanged as the acceptance criterion requires.

risks.risk: Changing the form's heading or its 'Add Visit' button text for the correction case introduces a new message key. I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails the build when a key in messages.properties is missing from any of the eight translated bundles, and it also fails on literal text in a template.
risks.mitigation: The narrowest reading is to leave createOrUpdateVisitForm.html unchanged — it already renders correctly for a non-new visit, since the 'New' block is guarded by ${visit['new']}. If wording is changed anyway, add the key to messages.properties and to every messages_*.properties except messages_en.

risks.risk: A visitId naming a visit on a different pet, or a petId under the wrong owner, is an identifier-tampering surface on a route with no authentication.
risks.mitigation: Resolve strictly by traversal — owner, then pet, then visit — and refuse anything the traversal does not find, with the IllegalArgumentException the factory already throws for a missing owner or pet. Recorded in docs/system-design.md Threat Model.

risks.risk: Visit inherits no equals override from BaseEntity, so pet.getVisits() is a LinkedHashSet keyed on identity. Re-adding or replacing the visit instance rather than mutating the loaded one would produce a duplicate row.
risks.mitigation: Mutate the instance the traversal returned. Do not construct a Visit on the correction path and do not call owner.addVisit(petId, visit) there.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records on the log, nothing to audit. No ADR authored for the design: the adjustment reuses PetController's established create-or-update shape with no alternative worth recording, which the adr-template skill excludes. The product decision is already recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-21-non-goal-visit-correction.md; its index row was missing from docs/adr/README.md and this dispatch added it, as the prd-entry flagged. docs/system-design.md edits: REQ-VISITEDIT-001 joined five Contracts rows, the VisitController purpose now names correction and its URL-only reach, the aggregate-invariant note states that a correction updates in place, and the identifier-tampering threat row records the traversal boundary. Open question carried forward, not resolved here: whether a visit whose date has passed should be correctable — docs/prd.md records it, and the narrowest reading (one date rule for every visit) is what this design implements. Ubiquitous language: 'Visit correction' is the term for the act, 'edit' names only the screen and the URL.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply-chain check not run: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle (plugins are java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management 1.1.7, graalvm native 1.1.2, cyclonedx 3.2.4, javaformat 0.0.47, nohttp 0.0.11), and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match was performed. processVisitCorrectionForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner and then saves it, so request parameters bind onto non-identifier Owner fields (firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone) on the correction POST, unvalidated. This is copied verbatim from the pre-existing processNewVisitForm, reaches nothing an attacker cannot already reach at /visits/new, and identifier binding stays disallowed, so it does not leave the application weaker than the recorded baseline. Worth noting only because a demonstration app is read and copied: a future round could take the visit alone and re-read the owner from the repository before saving.
approved_aspects: IDOR / identifier tampering closed by construction: loadPetWithVisit resolves the target strictly by graph traversal (owner.findById -> owner.getPet(petId) -> pet.getVisits() filtered by id) in VisitController.java:72-102, so a visitId naming a visit outside the addressed pet is refused rather than loaded. This matches the pattern PetController already uses (owner.getPet(petId)); a regression test covers it (theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitDoesNotBelongToThePet).

Mass assignment (security-principles row 3): the class-level @InitBinder disallowing 'id' and '*.id' covers the two new handlers, and the correction target comes from the path rather than a bound identifier, so no identifier is attacker-selectable past the traversal check. system-design.md threat-model row updated to state this.

Trusting cross-request state (security-principles row 10): every correction request re-resolves owner, pet, and visit from the repository and re-applies the full booking validation (rejectDateNotLaterThanToday plus @Valid), so no earlier request's validation is trusted.

Fail-secure on refusal: the validation-failure branch returns the form without calling owners.save; with spring.jpa.open-in-view=false the bound entity is detached, so an unvalidated in-place mutation cannot be flushed. Asserted by then(owners).should(never()).save(...).

Secret disclosure: no credential, token, connection string, or log statement is introduced. The new IllegalArgumentException message carries only visitId and petId, both int-typed path variables, so the error page reflects no attacker-controlled text.

Widening the exposed surface: the two new routes are documented in system-design.md (VisitController row, threat-model mass-assignment row) and the PRD, and they sit at the recorded no-auth/no-CSRF demonstration baseline rather than below it.
Supply chain: build.gradle and gradle/ are unchanged in the change set, so the diff adds no dependency and no new artifact source.
